replies.body:
Addressed in 7af97987b7380eddcbde82ddf6b7ed2316e92355.

Analysis: The cited helpers only wrapped short semantic convention conditionals, so they hid expected old and stable values at assertion sites. The same helper pattern also remained in Spring JMS 2.0. Inlining the selectors follows the test rule while preserving each mode's expected values. The RocketMQ destination helper remains because it performs a documented namespace derivation rather than only selecting an expected value.

Upsides: Every short mode-dependent expected value is visible where asserted, and the repository-wide cleanup includes the additional Spring JMS instance.

Downsides: The repeated conditionals make the tests longer.

replies.body: The PR description was ambiguous here. #19984 tracks the repository-wide cleanup, but this PR is only one incremental batch and does not close the issue. The cited Kafka helpers are outside this PR's scope and will remain for follow-up work. I updated the description to make that scope explicit.
